analysis.title: Nordic Alert: Complex risk landscape puts pressure on growth
key_insights: Global equities were nervous and volatile last week. The S&P 500 closed down 0.5% on Friday and the Nasdaq fell 0.2%. Both indices lost about 0.5% on the week, and the S&P 500 is up 11.4% in 2026.

SEB describes the risk backdrop as three items: high energy costs and El Niño raising inflation risks, an upward shift of the whole yield curve (cyclical, structural and political factors), and open questions about the sustainability of the AI boom. SEB says the scope for disappointment is greater than usual.
SEB says central banks' policy shift has kept long-term inflation expectations close to 2% targets. A rise in those expectations would be particularly troubling for bond markets and asset prices.

The Fed is expected to hold the policy rate at 4.00% on Wednesday, less than a week before the US midterm elections. Core PCE is 3.0% and not accelerating. Financial conditions have tightened on higher real yields and a modest equity pullback but remain accommodative.
SEB puts the probability of a rate hike on 9 December at just over 75%.
More than 110,000 people protested in Paris over the cost of living, with French authorities better prepared than before. Protests also occurred in Italy, Albania, Greece, Spain and Belgium.

SEB calls France's debt path unsustainable. Average debt maturity is 8.4 years, borrowing cost at that maturity is about 4.8%, long-term nominal GDP growth is about 3.0%, and productivity growth is weak. Moody's maintained France's rating, with warnings.

The ECB is expected to hold at 2.50% on Thursday. SEB flags two questions: whether Lagarde signals an early departure as ECB President, and whether the ECB is prepared to buy French government bonds. SEB's view is that the ECB should not shield French bonds from political risk premia.
Brazil's electoral court declared Lula da Silva the winner of the presidential run-off with 51.8% against 48.2% for Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro had not conceded at the time of writing.

Swedish Centre Party coalition talks are complicated at the national level. Carl Bildt said a snap election is the alternative to a major political shift. The budget bill is due 12 November and alternative budget motions 27 November. SEB does not expect negative market reactions.
Asian equity markets and equity futures were cautious early Monday ahead of the Fed and ECB decisions and new earnings reports.
earnings_insights: SEB says companies have delivered robust third-quarter earnings overall. No company-level figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The rate exceeds long-term nominal GDP growth of 3.0%, so the debt path is unsustainable without lower rates or deficits, or higher growth.
Growth below the borrowing cost, combined with deficits, drives the debt dynamics concern.
SEB forecasts a large jump in producer prices.
Consensus points to roughly flat sentiment.

French public debt trajectory with r (4.8%) above g (3.0%).

vol_and_positioning: Equity markets were nervous and volatile last week. SEB sees increased volatility as partly welcome because it reduces tunnel vision and herd mentality.

Brazil's run-off: Lula won and Flávio Bolsonaro had not conceded.
US midterm elections less than a week after the Fed decision.
Swedish government formation talks led by the Centre Party, with a possible snap election.
